summary: Integration testing of Sustainability Auto-Burn (1% post-transaction). Created /app/backend/tests/test_sustainability_burn_integration.py with 10 tests covering: (1) burn applied via real POST /api/bank-transfer/admin/mark-paid when balance > 30k, (2) NO burn below 30k threshold, (3) idempotency (no double-burn for same service_ref_id+service_type), (4) reverse_sustainability_burn restores balance + marks original reversed=true + inserts auto_burn_reversal credit, (5) GET /api/user/{uid}/redeem-limit total_redeemed EXCLUDES burns, (6) GET /api/prc-statement/usage-history/{uid} total_used EXCLUDES burns AND total_used == sum(by_category), (7) GET /api/bank-transfer/admin/requests loads under 5s (measured ~1.5s), (8) over_limit_only=true filter returns only pending rows with redeem_limit_raw < 0, (9) GET /api/admin/debug/total-redeemed/{uid} requires admin Bearer (401 without, 403 for non-admin, 200 for admin), (10) idempotency query is correctly keyed on (user_id, type, service_ref_id, service_type) — different service_type with same ref_id burns independently. Result: 10/10 PASSED. Live preview spot-check on UID cbdf46d7-7d66-4d43-8495-e1432a2ab071 confirms /redeem-limit total_redeemed=109609.0 == /usage-history summary.total_used=109609.0 == sum(by_category) (108609+500+500=109609). No 'Burn' category leaks into used breakdown. Pre-existing /app/backend/tests/test_sustainability_burn.py 5/5 unit tests pass when run individually (cross-test event-loop binding limitation in motor — non-functional).

minor.issue: Module-level `from server import db` binds motor client to the first test's event loop; subsequent async tests in same pytest run fail with 'Future attached to a different loop'. Tests pass individually. Suggested fix: parameterize each test with its own AsyncIOMotorClient (as the new integration test does) OR add session-scoped event_loop fixture in conftest. Non-blocking — feature itself works.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/sustainability_burn.py: Idempotency check is correctly keyed on (user_id, type=auto_burn, service_ref_id, service_type) — verified test_idempotency_query_shape that two different service_types with the same ref_id each burn independently. Good design.

routes/sustainability_burn.py: apply_sustainability_burn uses an atomic conditional update {prc_balance: {$gte: burn_amt}} to prevent overdraft from race conditions. Returns 'balance_changed_concurrent' on miss — robust.

routes/sustainability_burn.py: Refund flow (reverse_sustainability_burn) marks original entry reversed=true AND inserts a separate auto_burn_reversal credit entry. This provides audit trail + ensures statement shows both lines. Verified in test 4.
manual_bank_transfer.py:951-961: Burn hook runs AFTER status flip to 'paid' inside try/except — non-fatal failure won't block the mark-paid response. Good.

manual_bank_transfer.py:716-731: 15s parallel asyncio.gather + asyncio.wait_for around redeem-limit enrichment with absolute fallback to redeem_limit_available=None ensures the admin requests page always loads. Measured 1.5s in live preview.
Burn rate (1%) and threshold (30k) are module-level constants — fine for this size. If they ever become tenant-specific, move to admin_settings collection.

Live spot-check: /api/user/{uid}/redeem-limit `limit.total_redeemed` (109609) exactly matches /api/prc-statement/usage-history/{uid} `summary.total_used` (109609) which equals sum(by_category) — Home Dashboard 'USED' and 'Redeem Used Details' will stay in sync.

Minor: /api/admin/debug/total-redeemed expects header user_id-less Bearer JWT (decoded directly). Could optionally use the existing dependency injection pattern from get_current_admin for consistency, but current inline check is correct.

Run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://formula-audit-fix.preview.emergentagent.com MONGO_URL=mongodb://localhost:27017 DB_NAME=paras_reward_db pytest /app/backend/tests/test_sustainability_burn_integration.py -v --asyncio-mode=auto. rca of the issue: N/A — no defects in feature implementation. Two initial test failures in my new integration test were due to test code reading wrong response paths (data['used'] vs data['limit']['total_redeemed']; data['total_used'] vs data['summary']['total_used']). Fixed in the test; feature behavior was correct from the start.
